threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep trying to pet the therapy horse at the local park, but all the locals just laugh and say it’s for emergencies only.
Caught the 197 last night; an old bloke serenading the driver with sea shanties. The driver just chuckled, might’ve been the highlight of his shift.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I walked past the old Turkish market and heard a saxophonist jamming with a grandma selling baklava. That blend is Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find an entire outdoor gym made from repurposed playground equipment. It’s like CrossFit meets Kinderland.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their ability to dodge potholes while riding a bike—like it's an Olympic sport. The newbies aren’t quick enough.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a riptide of laughter when a toddler loudly asked why the bus smells like hot dogs and feet. True, little one, true.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think everyone’s in a rush, but around here, it’s normal to stop for a chat on the street. This neighborhood moves at its own pace.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot them at the market, struggling with the 'no bag' rule as they heap veggies into their backpacks, looking a bit lost.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for your coffee ‘to go’ instead of embracing the sit-and-savor vibe at the local cafés.
Heard a couple arguing about whether the chips from the late-night fish shop were worth the wait. She swore by the tartar sauce – typical Brixton debate!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids playing football in the street while the baker yelled to them to watch out for her croissants. Felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's normal to have outdoor screenings of obscure films right in the middle of the street. You catch a classic while sipping on a Berliner Weiße. Truly unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they gossip about the BART delays—it's practically a weather report these days. Newbies just look confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a guy serenaded the whole 19 bus with a ukulele. We all forgot about the delays and just sang along. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about bars and restaurants, but many miss the community art projects tucked between the façades.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still pull out a map instead of using their phone for directions—makes them stand out in Gràcia's winding streets.
